strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Unix Shell Execution in ICS

analytics.name: Analytic 2088
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies sh/bash/ash/zsh/BusyBox execution from an unexpected parent, unauthorized account, remote session, or non-approved script path, particularly when followed by OT-relevant network discovery, persistence, file modification, or communications. Alert only when the interpreter/shell is not expected for the asset role or user/service context, or when its parent, path, arguments, remote-session source, or follow-on behavior violates the approved OT baseline. Suppress approved engineering scripts, vendor support, diagnostics, backup, patching, and maintenance windows.

tuning.description: Approved shell paths and BusyBox use
Approved jump hosts and management subnets
High-risk shell commands and ICS-relevant follow-on activity

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve for shell/interpreter and child commands

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: auth.log/secure.log; SSH or console session context

analytics.name: Analytic 2089
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies network-device CLI or underlying Unix-like shell access from an unauthorized management source/account, followed by privileged or configuration commands outside an approved change window. Do not alert solely on CLI use. Require violation of the management matrix, command authorization, or change-control context.

tuning.description: Jump hosts, management VLANs, and administrative CIDRs
Enable/configure, ACL, route, NAT, firmware, file transfer, shell escape

log_sources.name: networkdevice:syslog
log_sources.channel: CLI command audit / configuration command history

analytics.name: Analytic 2090
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies shell/CLI access to an embedded controller, gateway, HMI appliance, or IoT/OT device from an unauthorized source/account, or command execution that is inconsistent with the device role and approved maintenance workflow. Require a session/command authorization violation or corroborating configuration/firmware/process effect; do not infer maliciousness from deterministic timing alone.

Firmware, configuration write/erase, service manipulation, shell escape
